To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nitridoosmium complexes are potent anti-cancer agents that are able to induce apoptosis in cancer cells, inhibit the growth of cancer cells in vitro and in mice xenograft models, induce G2/M-phase and S-phase arrest, form stable adducts with DNA and inhibit the activity of DNA polymerases.
the osmium(VI) nitrido complex [Os(V) (N)(sap)(H(2)O)(Cl)] (1) displays anti-cancer properties and induces apoptosis in human cancer cell lines.

the nitridoosmium complex [Os(V)(N)(sap)Cl(2)(OH(2))] is a new type of metal complex with anti-cancer activity, that it is the only osmium complex with anti-catalytic activity, and that the anti-cancer activity is due to its ability to inhibit the activity of the DNA polymerase.

the synthesis of novel osmium complexes, their structural characterization, and the evaluation of their biological activities.
the synthesis, structural characterisation and reactivity of new osmium complexes, with a particular emphasis on the chemistry of osmium(VI), which is the highest oxidation state of the osmium.
synthesis and characterisation of new complexes of osmium(VI) and osmium(IV) and their application in the area of medicinal chemistry.

the nitridoosmium complex is a new class of potent anti-cancer agents.

the nitridoosmium complexes display a unique mode of interaction with the DNA and the mechanism of action is different from the classical platinum drugs.
